headline: Use {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, the cheapest configuration over the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} pass-rate gate, though it clears it by only {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.gap|abs|pts} point.
lede: A fresh run of the same size would read it under the gate {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.wrong_side} of the time. {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} clears with room for {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_cost_gap|abs|usd_whole} more a month.
flag: The one rule set in advance is the overall pass-rate gate at {criteria.pass_rate.threshold}, read on point estimates; nothing declared a latency budget, a per-task floor or a price per point.

caveats.material_if: Material if the pick's true pass rate sits under the gate, which its clearance cannot rule out: then the high-reasoning Brisk-S configuration is the cheapest that passes. Cost, the other half of the call, is measured.

Material in the same direction: the pick is the cheapest of {n_candidates|words} readings to land over the line, so a fresh run tends to read it lower. It touches the high-reasoning alternative far less, since that reads {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.value}.

Material only for claims that one configuration beats another; the call reads each configuration against the gate and on cost, and the two Brisk-S survivors are compared unpaired, which reads wider than a paired comparison would.

decision.text: Ship {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} at {cost_per_1k.brisk-s.low.r1|usd_per_1k}, the cheapest of the {count.passing.pass_rate|words} configurations over the gate.

Atlas-M passes only with low or high reasoning, and its cheapest passing configuration, {arm:atlas-m.low.r1}, costs {cost_per_1k.atlas-m.low.r1|usd_per_1k}; where it passes, its pass rate is not separated from Brisk-S at the same settings.
Nano-XS misses the gate at every setting; its best, {arm:nano-xs.high.r1}, reads {measure.pass_rate.nano-xs.high.r1.mean}, a miss more cases would only confirm.

The pick's clearance is the weakest margin on the page and is too thin for more cases to settle: about {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.cases_needed|int} cases would give even odds of clearing it. If the gate must hold beyond noise, ship {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} instead; it buys clearance of the line, not a measured gain over the pick.

Multi-hop questions ({task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean}) and ambiguous entities ({task.disamb.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean}) are the pick's weak tasks; the gate reads overall, so it does not see them.
The gate's owner says whether the gate must hold beyond noise or on the point estimate: that alone chooses between the two Brisk-S configurations.

claims.text: Of {n_candidates|words} configurations, {count.passing.pass_rate|words} reach the gate, and {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} is the cheapest of them at {cost_per_1k.brisk-s.low.r1|usd_per_1k}.

evidence.caption: Pass rate, cost per 1,000 calls, p95 latency and gate status for every model, reasoning level and retry setting.

claims.text: Its clearance sits inside the noise: a fresh run would read it under the gate {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.wrong_side} of the time, against {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.overall.wrong_side} for {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}.

evidence.caption: The {count.passing.pass_rate|words} configurations over the gate and the nearest misses under it. This block draws no interval: the snapshot states none per configuration, and the binomial spread behind the re-run odds in the sentence is not one it can draw.

claims.text: Clearing the gate with room means {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} at {cost_per_1k.brisk-s.high.r1|usd_per_1k}, or {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_cost_gap|abs|usd_whole} more a month at today's volume, and it buys no pass-rate gain separated from the pick's ({compare.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval|interval} points).

evidence.caption: Cost per 1,000 calls for the configurations on the cost frontier; log scale.
Latency from p50 to p95 for the same configurations; high-reasoning Brisk-S also has the longer tail, and no budget was declared.

claims.text: Read task by task, with no per-task counts or floor, the pick sits under the gate's level on multi-hop questions ({task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean}) and ambiguous entities ({task.disamb.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean}), while {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} reads at or above it in each task.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task for the two Brisk-S survivors; descriptive, with no per-task floor declared.
A miss from the pick's weakest task: it collapsed two hops into one search.

claims.text: One retry is what lifts Brisk-S over the gate: at low reasoning it moves the pass rate from {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0.mean} to {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean}, a gain whose interval is {lever.retry.brisk-s.low.r0.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.interval|interval} points.

evidence.caption: Brisk-S's configurations against the gate; only those with a retry at low and high reasoning reach it.

explore.binds: Which configuration is the cheapest over it.
explore.outcome: At a gate up to {criteria.pass_rate.nano-xs.off.r0.value} the pick is {arm:nano-xs.off.r0}; up to {criteria.pass_rate.nano-xs.off.r1.value}, {arm:nano-xs.off.r1}; up to {criteria.pass_rate.nano-xs.low.r1.value}, {arm:nano-xs.low.r1}; up to {criteria.pass_rate.nano-xs.high.r1.value}, {arm:nano-xs.high.r1}; up to {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0.value}, {arm:brisk-s.low.r0}; up to {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.value}, {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}; up to {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.value}, {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}; up to {criteria.pass_rate.atlas-m.high.r1.value}, {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}; above that nothing passes.

explore.control: Price of a pass-rate point a month
explore.binds: Which frontier configuration is worth its cost, if the owner prices points instead of holding the gate.
explore.outcome: Under {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point|usd_whole} a point the low-reasoning pick holds; up to {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point|usd_whole}, high-reasoning Brisk-S; above that, {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}. Neither step's gain is separated from zero, so these prices are point readings with no bounded ends.

next.text: The gate's owner declares whether the gate must hold beyond noise or on the point estimate.
next.settles: Which Brisk-S configuration ships: on the point estimate the low-reasoning pick, beyond noise the high-reasoning one. More cases can't settle the pick's clearance at any practical size.

next.text: Re-run only the two Brisk-S survivors on a fresh set of cases the size of today's.
next.settles: It gives each a second reading free of the selection among {n_candidates|words}, which is the figure a point-estimate gate should be read on. It does not settle the pick against the line: at that size a fresh run reads it under the gate {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.wrong_side} of the time even if today's figure is the truth.

next.text: Give low-reasoning Brisk-S an explicit hop-by-hop plan for multi-hop questions and re-run.
next.settles: Whether the cheapest configuration can clear the gate with room, removing the need to pay for high reasoning.

method.text: {scoreboard.brisk-s.low.r1.cases|int} cases per configuration across {count.tasks|words} tasks; the snapshot states no repeats and no per-task counts.
The snapshot doesn't define what makes a trial pass; failures are classed as a missing call, wrong arguments, a wrong tool or malformed output.
Overall pass rate at or above {criteria.pass_rate.threshold}, the one criterion declared, read on each configuration's point estimate.

The snapshot states no interval on any pass rate. Spreads come from each rate's binomial count. Two configurations are compared unpaired, which reads wider than a paired comparison. Re-run odds and case counts are a normal approximation at {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.level}.
Read between configurations that differ in retry alone, unpaired, at {lever.retry.brisk-s.low.r0.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.level}.
Cost per 1,000 calls as measured; monthly figures at {meta.volume_per_month|int} calls a month.
No control or production configuration; no latency budget; no more than one retry; no judge appears in the snapshot.

The pass-rate dot plot draws no interval because no block over pass rates can draw the binomial spread; the re-run odds carry it in the sentence instead. Per-task rates carry no counts, so every per-task reading is descriptive.
